newsitem.title: UK: NWE gas oil spreads ease, trade inactive.
newsitem.headline: NWE gas oil spreads ease, trade inactive.

text.p: European gas oil differentials were slightly easier on Monday but lack of arbitrage and a seasonal summer lull stalled business, traders said.
Outright prices slid $1 a tonne during the day. August IPE finished at $162.50 a tonne, pulled $1 lower by losses in crude.
"It's just dead out there," one trader said.
Two 20,000 tonne low sulphur diesel flexi cargoes for late July/early August were offered at $4.25 and $4.50 over August IPE, attracting a bid of $3.75 over. But no trade was agreed.
Russian heating oil was seen at flat to 50 cents over August IPE, some 50 cents down.
Supply was seen ample ahead of the annual shutdown at Ventpsils.
Some traders said German heating oil saw an unusually wide spread between bid and offer, with a notional bid at 50 cents over August IPE and offers around $2.50 over the screen.
The key ARA barge market was also quiet in the absence of inland demand for heating oil and amid trader caution ahead of further news about the resumption of Iraqi oil exports.
Prompt heating oil was around 25/50 cents over August IPE, with first half August 25 cents dearer.
Low sulphur diesel was offered at a premium to August IPE of $4.25 for Flushing and $4.75 for Rotterdam.
